# Fixed strings law/engineering-code.md, the code rules that load on a code read, must carry, one
# per line; read by tests/short-law.test.sh. A line starting with # is a comment.
# caps
3 parameters
3 levels of nesting
# bans
`biome-ignore`
`eslint-disable`
`@ts-ignore`
`@ts-expect-error`
`@ts-nocheck`
`istanbul ignore`
`c8 ignore`
`v8 ignore`
non-null `!`
`catch (e) {}`
`.catch(() => {})`
`except: pass`
discarded into `_`
inline `interface` or `type` of 2+ properties
`*.types`
`TypeError`
`RangeError`
`RuntimeException`
`Promise.reject(new Error(...))`
`.only`
`fit`
`fdescribe`
`.skip`
`xit`
`xdescribe`
`test.todo`
`debugger`
`console.*`
# one thing per file
`*.constants`
`*.config`
`*.schema`
`*.styles`
read 2.3 before creating any file or folder
# principles
second caller
paste the search that found none
Leave nothing behind
Dead code that was there before your change is a follow-up
# clean-code floor
does or answers, never both
No flag parameters
Never mutate inputs
Fail fast at the boundary
One level of abstraction per function
Talk to what you hold
keeps its cause and context
awaited, returned or handled
Composition before inheritance
A closed set is a type
# refuse on sight
Add error handling later
a `TODO` with no owner
commented-out code
zero references
# performance guardrails
Never query or call per loop item
Parallelize independent I/O
Bound every result set
Bound every cache
Bound every fan-out
No sync blocking I/O
Filter on indexes
No O(n²) on unbounded input
Batch bulk writes
Stream large payloads
Stable props and keys in UI hot paths
before optimizing
# four principles
Think before coding
Simplicity first
Surgical changes
Goal-driven execution
never loosened to pass
never hunks of this diff
# the edit guard prompts; the user's yes is the exception, kept on the line
The edit guard turns
permission prompt
`law-exception: <what the technology needs>`
never route around it
# names (the short form of the placement guide's symbol table and refused names)
where the language, its frameworks and the codebase set no convention
`PascalCase` types, classes, interfaces (no `I` prefix), enums and UI components
`camelCase` functions, methods, variables and parameters, and `useCamelCase` hooks
`SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` enum members and true module constants (a computed default stays `camelCase`)
Booleans start with `is`/`has`/`can`/`should`, functions with a verb
private fields use the language's own marker (a leading `_` only where it has none)
a file's name and its primary export agree
Refused as a whole name: `data`, `info`, `item`, `obj`, `temp`, `val`, `res`, `result`, `handle`, `process`, `manager`, `helper`, `util(s)`, `base`, `core`, `MyThing`, `ThingImpl` or `AbstractThing` with one implementation
any name that needs the body or a comment to explain it
